newsitem.title: FRANCE: Framatome head sceptical of GEC-Alsthom merger.
newsitem.headline: Framatome head sceptical of GEC-Alsthom merger.

text.p: The president of French nuclear engineering group Framatome has expressed scepticism about a possible merger with Franco-British joint venture GEC-Alsthom, the French Senate said on Thursday.

Jean-Claude Leny "believed that the argument of industrial synergy given to justify the planned merger with GEC-Alsthom did not stand up to an examination...of the activities of the two groups," it said.
A Senate statement said Leny told its economic affairs commission on Wednesday that Framatome "has no debts, is going well and has no need of urgent restructuring."

"Jean-Claude Leny also cautioned of the threats that, according to him, this (merger) would cause for the continued existence of the French nuclear branch and, by extension, on the energy independence of France," it said.
And Leny cautioned that a link with Britain could upset cooperation with Germany.

Leny said he was informed of the possible merger on August 30, the day the French state publicly gave the green light for merger talks between Framatome and GEC-Alsthom, a joint venture of Alcatel Alsthom and GEC Plc.
The major owners of Framatome are Alcatel with 44 percent, state owned CEA (36), electricity utility EDF (11) and the Consortium de Realisation (four).
